counterfactual_missing_items: No captured disconfirming ECG finding that would refute atrial tachycardia
Positive SARS-CoV-2 alone does not specify a cardiac arrhythmia mechanism
decisive_items: Regular, narrow complex tachycardia with rate of 170 beats/min
Superiorly directed P waves (negative in leads II, III, and aVF)
Long RP interval (RP interval > PR interval)
response.rationale: R2 is uniquely supported by the ECG pattern: regular narrow complex tachycardia, superiorly directed P waves, and long RP interval are direct, specific markers of atrial tachycardia. R3 mentions COVID-19 but lacks arrhythmia ECG specificity; R1 explains pulmonary findings but not the palpitations/tachycardia; R4 uses the nonspecific echo finding of diastolic dysfunction and does not account for the ECG criteria.

rejected.why: Only links COVID-19 infection to a generic arrhythmia without engaging the highly specific atrial tachycardia ECG pattern.
Explains cough, PCR positivity, and crackles as pneumonia, but does not address the narrow complex tachycardia, P-wave axis, or RP interval.
Mild diastolic dysfunction is nonspecific and does not explain the regular narrow complex tachycardia with long RP interval and superior P waves.
